subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Which lifecycle hook surface should own subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call-threshold behavior, and what data or permissions may those hooks receive?
rationale: The code proves a missing surface, but the safe boundary between workspace/internal hooks, typed plugin hooks, threshold configuration, and sensitive run data is a maintainer API/security decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Stage observation-only internal hooks first
options.body: Add narrowly scoped workspace/internal observation events for subagent and turn completion while leaving threshold stopping and result rewriting out of the first contract.

options.title: Keep this plugin-only
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers decide lifecycle observability with subagent/tool data belongs only to typed code plugins.

options.title: Design a combined lifecycle API
options.body: Create one explicit split between internal workspace events and typed plugin control hooks before implementation starts.

recommendation.title: Stage observation-only internal hooks first
recommendation.body: Add narrowly scoped workspace/internal observation events for subagent and turn completion while leaving threshold stopping and result rewriting out of the first contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is primarily about the typed plugin hook contract and adjacent guard/subagent hook semantics where this person has recent relevant history.
